c.tagline: A lagoon town on the Garden Route framed by dramatic sandstone Heads and ancient indigenous forest

card: Widely accepted in town; cash useful for markets and smaller township eateries

taxi.fare: Negotiated or metered depending on operator
taxi.fareNote: Confirm the fare or use a ride-hailing app rather than hailing an unmarked taxi

emergency.note: 112 from any mobile phone reaches all emergency services

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: The waterfront and central Knysna are walkable; the Heads, forests, and outlying beaches require a car or organized tour

safety.safety: Generally safe for tourists in the central and waterfront areas, though petty crime occurs as in most South African towns
safety.crime: Avoid isolated areas after dark and secure valuables; township areas require a local guide

hood_landmark.Knysna Central / Waterfront: The Knysna Quays waterfront shopping and dining complex
hood_landmark.Leisure Isle: Leisure Isle's lagoon-front beaches and sailing club
hood_landmark.The Heads: The Western and Eastern Heads lookout points over the lagoon mouth
hood_landmark.Brenton-on-Sea: Brenton-on-Sea's beach and Featherbed Nature Reserve views

avoid.reason: Avoid walking in the townships north of the N2 without a local guide.
Lock cars and hide valuables at trailheads and viewpoints, and avoid walking after dark away from the waterfront.

hood_desc: The commercial heart of town along the lagoon, with the Knysna Quays complex, restaurants, and oyster bars; the natural base for most visitors.
A upscale canal-front marina development a short drive from downtown, popular for its restaurants and waterfront apartments.
A residential peninsula jutting into the lagoon with quiet beaches and lawn-fringed streets, good for a calmer stay.
The dramatic sandstone cliffs flanking the lagoon's narrow entrance to the sea, essential for photos and sunset views.
A small beach village west of Knysna with dramatic coastal views over the Featherbed Nature Reserve, better for a peaceful coastal stay than nightlife.

water.note: Municipal tap water is safe; occasional drought restrictions apply.

transit.sys: No formal municipal bus network; minibus taxis serve local routes
transit.hours: Minibus taxis run roughly daylight hours
transit.map: Not centrally published; ask locally for minibus taxi routes
transit.note: Most visitors rent a car, since Garden Route sights are spread out along the N2

transport.air: George Airport (GRJ), about 1 hr drive; Cape Town International (CPT) is roughly 5 hr away by car
transport.train: No passenger rail service to Knysna
transport.bus: Greyhound, Intercape, and Baz Bus (backpacker hop-on-hop-off) connect along the Garden Route
transport.car: A rental car is strongly recommended for exploring the Garden Route; driving is on the left

airport.name: George Airport
airport.transport: Rental car, pre-booked transfer, or shuttle

net.m: Good 4G coverage in town, patchier in forest areas
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Vodacom or MTN tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: 10% is customary for tour guides and drivers
